items.summary: Anthropic, maker of Claude, began trading on Nasdaq under ticker ANT midday Thursday at $111.50 per share, a 34 percent rise from its final IPO price; it later dipped to $95.69 and closed at $97.17, still nearly 17 percent above the offering price. The company had initially planned to offer 825 million shares in the range of $70-$78 but on Wednesday raised that to 980 million shares at $83 each; it is valued at $2 trillion and its debut surpassed SpaceX's as history's largest IPO, per Al Jazeera. Demand was strong: Founders ETF portfolio manager Michael Monaghan said books were well oversubscribed with high-quality orders (attributed to him). The listing is the first of two major AI labs going public on US markets; competitor OpenAI has also eyed an IPO. Analyst Dan Ives called it a big near-term win for tech that should help restore investor confidence in the growth thesis, while IPOX's Lukas Muehlbauer noted some demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out even if long-term profitability remains uncertain (attributed to them). Anthropic disclosed a net loss of $104bn in the first nine months of 2026 and devoted about 90 pages of its roughly 300-page SEC filing to risks, including warnings that its systems could pose catastrophic or existential risks. A group of AI safety experts released the 'Misanthropic Statement' around the IPO, stating Anthropic is not a safe company; CEO Dario Amodei responded via X that he would pace training and deployment until confident in safety and human control (attributed to him). The listing also drew attention because Anthropic has committed $110bn to Amazon for computing infrastructure and at least $121.3bn to Google, while Nvidia invested a combined $20bn including amounts tied to the IPO.
items.title: Anthropic's record-setting IPO opened amid safety backlash

items.summary: At the Ficci AGM, PM Modi admonished the corporate sector for not passing reduced corporate tax to employees through higher wages or more hiring. He cited that the basic corporate tax rate fell from 30% in 2014 to 22%, and income up to Rs 12 lakh is now exempt; he asked whether companies raised salaries or headcount, attributing their reluctance to greed. Modi said individual tax relief boosted consumption while reduced GST rates and faster I-T refunds freed money previously stuck for months. The remarks came amid fresh demands for budget sops as business leaders submitted a wish list to the finance minister. Businesses cited cost pressure and weakening demand despite signs of an investment pick-up, though this is reported rather than attributed by Modi. Beyond tax, Modi urged industry captains to propose reforms without inhibition, seize trade-agreement opportunities, promote domestic manufacturing in pharma, steel and aluminium, build capability in pharmaceutical ingredients, invest in agriculture, enter strategic areas, and make 'India First' the foundation of long-term investment decisions over the next 20 years. No figures beyond those quoted are reported.
items.title: Modi rebukes industry over unpassed corporate tax cuts

items.summary: Cyclone Akvan is forecast to make landfall as a cyclonic storm along the Odisha coast between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon or afternoon, per IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra (attributed), with wind speeds of 90-100 kmph. The system was about 410 km from Gopalpur and 470 km from Puri on Thursday evening, moving at 13 kmph according to an IMD official. By Thursday evening, PTI reported quoting Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil that 2,98,676 people had been evacuated across the state; Odisha has set up 2,523 relief camps and prepared 9,341 cyclone shelters (of which CM Mohan Charan Majhi said 2,623 are operational), with 423 rescue teams deployed. Neighbouring Andhra Pradesh received red alerts for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, orange for Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli, and yellow for Kakinada; at Paradip Port six fishing boats carrying 54 fishermen were given safe harbour (ANI), while Balasore identified shelters to relocate 12,000-15,000 people with a contingency plan up to 2.5 lakh if required. Rail services were disrupted—East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29, South Eastern Railway cancelled 28 express trains—and tourist sites including Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika were barred; several temples and national parks in Puri remained closed on specific November dates. Tripura is expected to see scattered rain and isolated thunderstorms from Akvan's outer cloud bands (IMD), with the IMD ruling out any direct cyclone strike or severe winds there. All figures are forecasts or reported preparations attributed to their sources; no casualties, damage, or confirmed landfall occurred.
items.title: Odisha braces for Cyclone Akvan landfall between Puri and Gopalpur, with nearly 3 lakh evacuated

items.summary: During pre-budget consultations with finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, energy and infrastructure representatives urged measures for the Union budget due on 1 February 2027. Alok Kumar of the All India Discoms Association (AIDA) said key recommendations included improving power reliability to encourage distribution-network investment, ensuring timely subsidy payments from state governments to discoms, lowering import duties on battery energy storage systems, and reducing GST to about 5% or zero. Currently BESS attract a 20% basic customs duty with an 18% GST rate; the cut is sought until domestic manufacturing capacity expands. Separately, in an October letter to the ministry of new and renewable energy, the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) called for correcting an inverted tax structure on graphite anodes: a 10% basic customs duty on key raw materials versus 2.5% on finished products makes imports cheaper than domestic production, raising costs and eroding margins; NSEFI proposed either raising the duty on finished anodes to 10% or reducing it on raw materials to 2.5%. Finance ministry queries remained unanswered at publication.
items.title: Energy sector seeks lower battery import duties in FY28 budget

items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India's shares closed 5% higher, trading 24% above their Rs 1,785 issue price following a September 24, 2026 market debut. The rally follows several brokerages initiating coverage with 'buy' ratings; Anand Rathi Research set a target price of Rs 2,381, implying about 7% upside from current levels (attributed to the brokerage). Renewed large-cap interest is being attributed by Nuvama's report to small and mid caps lagging on profit growth after four consecutive quarters of outperformance. In Q2 FY27, large-caps' profit growth exceeded smaller peers by more than 25%, with manufacturing-focused small- and mid-caps facing margin pressure while banks, IT and industrials continued to outperform (attributed to Nuvama). The article's 'hold or sell' framing is editorial rather than an analyst recommendation; the author is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst. No table of figures appears in the item.
items.title: NSE stock rallies on brokerage 'buy' ratings and large-cap rotation

items.summary: Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 policy meeting, released Wednesday, show officials raised concerns that heavy borrowing tied to artificial intelligence could destabilize the financial system. Reuters reported these worries were part of a broader assessment in which elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage ranked among the most significant risks, while strong balance sheets at banks and households offered some protection against severe shocks. Officials worried AI investment returns might disappoint expectations, that much related debt flowed through opaque financing structures, and that concentration across a small number of companies could let setbacks to major players ripple into markets and the economy. The discussion also touched measures to harden resilience: raising bank capital requirements, ensuring lenders can reach the Fed's emergency discount window during stress, and possibly creating an asset-purchasing mechanism for financial stability risks; Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack advocated a temporary programme with an exit strategy, while others cautioned against using monetary policy for market disruptions. Nearly all policymakers said further interest rate increases may be needed if conditions hold as expected, though rates were held unchanged at the October meeting amid persistent inflation concerns.
items.title: Fed minutes flag AI-driven financial stability risks

items.summary: Reuters reported that New Delhi is applying total duties of 162.5%, partly payable via bank guarantees, to bulk Scotch imports the day before an India-UK trade agreement came into effect in July; this rate exceeds the 150% levy previously in place and reverses anticipated margin benefits from lower import costs under the pact. New Delhi asserts that bulk Scotch is a raw material for other products and does not qualify for reduced tariffs, marking what Reuters frames as the first major dispute under the agreement. Shares of Indian whisky makers fell on Thursday: United Spirits (Diageo's Indian unit) dropped more than 4% in early trading before narrowing losses, Radico Khaitan around 3.5%, and Allied Blenders and Distillers more than 2%. Pernod Ricard is not listed in India but its French shares fell after the story was published on Wednesday, as did Diageo's London-listed shares; ICICI Securities said the higher levy could stress margins and working capital. The British government responded that ministers are working with India to resolve the dispute, while an Indian statement following a visit by Prince William and Kate noted Modi welcomed momentum in bilateral relations without confirming whether the Scotch issue was discussed.
items.title: India's 162.5% bulk Scotch tariff weighs on Indian liquor stocks after India-UK pact dispute

items.summary: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday, with the S&P500 dropping 2% to mark its sixth straight day of losses—the index's longest such run in two and a half years. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points (2.2%) and closed at 49,097.06, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.69 points (2.3%) to 23,879.20; more than 90% of S&P500 stocks ended lower. The index is now 8.2% below its record high from last month. Anthropic's IPO on the Nasdaq initially lifted sentiment—shares opened above $115 after pricing at $83, higher than the earlier expected range of $70 to $78—but closed at $97.17, up 17.1% from its offering price; the brief S&P500 gain of as much as 1.3% did not persist. Several AI-linked stocks reversed early gains: Micron ended 2.1% lower after an initial rise of 7.8%, CoreWeave fell 6.1% after a morning jump of 10.5%, and Nvidia closed 3.3% down after erasing an early gain of 4.7%. The selling reflects concerns about elevated valuations, expensive borrowing under high interest rates, whether AI investments will generate sufficient returns, possible regulatory pressure following Democratic midterm gains, and the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year US Treasury slipped to 5.04% from 5.07%. Elsewhere, Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.7% (aided by a 4.6% gain in SoftBank Group) and South Korea's Kospi gained 1.4%, while Germany's DAX fell 1.1%. Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives described the conditions as 'a very turbulent, white-knuckle period.'
items.title: S&P500 posts its longest losing streak in two and a half years as AI-linked shares fall
